From the drawing to an open study

  1. Seven nodes on the PFDone design intent each; N4 is the worked node

Why this deck

A HAZOP asks one question, node by node

The OTS (operator training simulator) runs this unit. Now: what can go wrong?

HAZOP

Hazard and operability study: guide words applied to each node's intent.

PHA Studio

The program holding the study. PHA = process hazard analysis.

OTS link

A green ▶ OTS chip runs the row on the DCS console.

IEC 61882 = the international HAZOP standard; PFD = process flow diagram; DCS = distributed control system.

Interactive · click a node

Seven nodes, one design intent each

Each node is the equipment that serves one intent; N4 meters resin into the air, so feed deviations start there.

The worked node

N4: day silo D-100 and rotary feeder RV-101

Its intent: meter 18 t/h of resin into the pressurised line and seal the air.

WI-110
resin feed rate on the D-100 load cells
18 t/h
HIC-110
hand set point of the RV-101 speed
60 %
PT-102
air pressure at the pick-up
47 kPa g
PIC-102
override: cuts the feed above this pressure
58 kPa g
PSHH-102
trip I-1 stops RV-101 (same PT-102)
70 kPa g
XI-106
$v/v_{salt}$ after the line step; design value
1.24 (–)

$v_{salt}$ = saltation velocity (m/s): below it resin drops out of the air and forms dunes and plugs.

Before the first row

Read a tag in two seconds

Every safeguard in the worksheet is a tag. The letters follow ISA 5.1 (the instrument symbol standard).

P F W L T
first letter: pressure, flow, weight, level, temperature
PT-102, WI-110
X
first letter: a computed value
XI-106 = v/vsalt
I, C, H
indicator, controller, hand set
PIC-102, HIC-110
A + H / L
alarm high or low (HI, LO on the DCS)
PAH-102, WAH-110
SHH
switch high-high: an automatic trip
PSHH-102 → I-1
PSV, DV, FIC
pressure safety valve, diverter valve, flow controller
PSV-101, DV-103

Steps 1 and 2

Name the study, the team and the nodes first

Part 1 opened the program. Before any row, fix who and what.

  • Study: title, scope D-100 → D-201A/B
  • Team: leader, scribe, process, operations, control
  • Documents: P&ID rev B, C&E, relief summary
  • Nodes: read the intent aloud first

The HAZOP move

A deviation is a parameter bent by a guide word

Parameter
a quantity of the intent: flow, pressure, level, speed
from the list
Guide word
how it departs: NO, MORE, LESS, REVERSE, AS WELL AS, OTHER THAN
IEC 61882
Deviation
the pair applied to this node's intent
one row
$\text{Flow} + \text{MORE} \;\Rightarrow\;$ too much resin for the air

Only pairs the team finds credible become rows; the rest are noted as considered.

Risk ranking

Two scales, one product

$S$
severity of the worst credible consequence, without safeguards
1–5
$L$
likelihood with the existing safeguards
1–5
$R$
risk rank; its band sets the action
1–25
$$R = S \times L$$

Bands: Low 1–4, Medium 5–9, High 10–16, Very high 17–25 (teaching matrix of this unit).

Interactive · move S and L

Where does a row land, and what must you do?

From the previous slide$R = S \times L$

One step in L moves N4.1 from Medium 9 to High 12: the band, not the number, decides the action.

LOPA · the quantities

Six numbers describe one scenario

LOPA replaces the L judgment with frequencies. An IPL is an independent protection layer.

$f_{IE}$
frequency of the initiating event (the cause)
per year
$P_{E}$
probability the enabling condition is present
0–1
$P_{CM}$
conditional modifier, e.g. people present
0–1
$PFD_j$
probability IPL $j$ fails on demand
0–1
$TEL$
tolerable event likelihood for severity $S$
per year
$f_{mit}$
frequency left after every IPL has acted
per year

LOPA derivation

How often the harm would happen with no IPLstep 1 of 3

$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE}$several causes add: any one starts it
$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \times \prod P_{E}$the cause harms only when conditions allow
$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \times \prod P_{E} \times \prod P_{CM}$and only if people are there

$f_{unmit}$ = unmitigated frequency (per year): the harm rate before any IPL acts.

LOPA derivation

Each IPL lets through only its failuresstep 2 of 3

Step 1$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \times \prod P_{E} \times \prod P_{CM}$
$f_{after\,1} = f_{unmit} \times PFD_1$only demands IPL 1 fails pass on
$f_{mit} = f_{unmit} \times \prod_j PFD_j$independent failures multiply

Valid only if each IPL is independent of the cause and of the other IPLs.

LOPA derivation

Compare with the tolerable likelihoodstep 3 of 3

Step 2$f_{mit} = f_{unmit} \times \prod_j PFD_j$
$RRF = f_{mit} \,/\, TEL$how many times too frequent
$RRR = TEL \,/\, f_{mit} = 1/RRF$PFD one more layer must reach

RRF = risk reduction factor still missing; RRR = required risk reduction. Both "None" when $f_{mit} \le TEL$.

Check the equations on a published case

The PHAWorks example, by hand

Steps 1–3$f_{mit} = \sum f_{IE} \prod P_E \prod P_{CM} \prod PFD_j \qquad RRF = f_{mit}/TEL$
$f_{mit} = 10^{-2} \times 5 \times 0.5 \times 0.5 \times 1 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^{-1} = 1.25\times10^{-5}$cause, factors, two IPLs
$RRF = 1.25\times10^{-5} / 10^{-6} = 12.5,\quad RRR = 0.08$TEL $10^{-6}$ per year

PHA Studio reproduces these numbers in the scenario dialog.

Example 3.1 · problem statement

EXAMPLE 3.1Row N4.5: pick-up pressure high

Row N4.5 of the worked example is Pressure MORE at the pick-up (PT-102), severity S = 4. Cause: a plug forms in the line (lumps at the bends, air below the saltation margin), 0.1 per year. People are near the line, E-101 or the blower when it bursts with probability 0.5. The safeguards on the row are:

SafeguardTypePFD
PAH-102 alarm 60 kPa gAlarm—
PIC-102 override 58 kPa gBPCS control0.1
PSHH-102 → I-1 (same PT-102)Trip—
PSV-101 90 kPa g, blower dischargeRelief0.01

TEL for S = 4 is $10^{-5}$ per year. (a) Which safeguards can be credited as IPLs? (b) Find $f_{unmit}$ and $f_{mit}$. (c) Are the IPLs enough? Give RRF and RRR.

Example 3.1 · solution (a)

EXAMPLE 3.1Which safeguards are IPLs?step 1 of 2

An IPL must be independent of the cause and of the other credited layers.

SafeguardCreditWhy
PIC-102 overrideIPL, 0.1basic process control (BPCS) layer; acts on the feed
PSV-101IPL, 0.01mechanical, needs no sensor
PSHH-102 → I-1noshares PT-102 with PIC-102
PAH-102nosame PT-102; operator response

Example 3.1 · solution (b) and (c)

EXAMPLE 3.1A gap of five timesstep 2 of 2

Steps 1–3$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \prod P_E \prod P_{CM} \quad f_{mit} = f_{unmit}\prod PFD_j \quad RRF = f_{mit}/TEL$
$f_{unmit} = 0.1 \times 1 \times 0.5 = 0.05$ per yearno enabling condition, so $P_E = 1$
$f_{mit} = 0.05 \times 0.1 \times 0.01 = 5\times10^{-5}$ per yearPIC-102 and PSV-101 only
$RRF = 5\times10^{-5}/10^{-5} = \mathbf{5},\quad RRR = \mathbf{0.2}$$f_{mit} > TEL$: not enough

One more IPL with PFD ≤ 0.2 closes the gap: R04 gives PSHH-102 its own transmitter.

Interactive · LOPA calculator, set to row N4.5

Add or remove a layer and watch the gap

Crediting PSHH-102 on its own transmitter (R04) gives $f_{mit} = 5\times10^{-6} \le 10^{-5}$: independence, not more alarms, closes the gap.

Full edition · LOPA scenario dialog

The same nine steps, done by the program

Your hand result should match line 9 of the dialog.

  • Tick IPLs from the row's own safeguards
  • Library values: teaching defaults in the style of the Center for Chemical Process Safety (CCPS)
  • Red cell: gap; green: meets TEL

Interactive · Full → Scenario Groups

Scenarios that hurt the same people add up

Group check$\sum f_{mit} \le$ group tolerance

Three rows that each meet $10^{-5}$ can fail it together: the receptor sees the sum, not each row.

Class Activity · Problems

Can you solve it yourself?

Class Activity · the plan

Two problems on the worked node

  1. Problem 4.1 · read an OTS runpractises Part 2: does test T01 support the rank of N4.1?
  2. Problem 4.2 · LOPA after R04practises Part 3: does an own transmitter for PSHH-102 close the gap?
  3. Then the critical-thinking quizten questions across all three parts, voted live

Problem 4.1 · statement · read first

PROBLEM 4.1Does the run support the rank of N4.1?

Row N4.1 (Flow MORE, too much resin for the air) is ranked S = 3, L = 3 with safeguards PIC-102 override 58 kPa g, XI-106 alarm, WAH-110 21 t/h and PSHH-102 → I-1 (70 kPa g). Test T01 pushes HIC-110 to 85 %. The DCS panel reports, 3:54 after the push:

TagDesignNow
WI-110 (t/h)17.9923.41
PT-102 (kPa g)47.358.1
XI-106 $v/v_{salt}$1.241.02

First alarms: XI-106 LO at 0:07, WI-110 HI at 0:16. Safety instrumented system (SIS): no trip. (a) Which safeguards acted? (b) How much margin to saltation is left? (c) Do the run's results support L = 3 and recommendation R01?

Problem 4.1 · solution

PROBLEM 4.1Two alarms and an override, no trip

$\text{margin} = v/v_{salt} - 1$

$v$ = air velocity after the step (m/s); $v_{salt}$ = saltation velocity (m/s).

(a) XI-106 LO, WAH-110, PIC-102 at 58 kPa gPSHH-102 at 70 never reached
(b) $1.02 - 1 = 0.02$, against $0.24$ at design2 % left before resin drops out
(c) L = 3 holds; R01 adds air with feedonly alarms and BPCS protect the margin

Problem 4.1 · try it

PROBLEM 4.1How close is the line to saltation?

Problem 4.1$\text{margin} = v/v_{salt} - 1$

T01 leaves 2 % against 24 % at design: the feed push uses up nearly all the margin before any trip acts.

Problem 4.2 · statement · read first

PROBLEM 4.2LOPA on N4.5 after recommendation R04

From Example 3.1 Row N4.5, S = 4: plug forming 0.1 per year; people present 0.5; IPLs PIC-102 override (PFD 0.1) and PSV-101 (PFD 0.01); TEL $10^{-5}$ per year.

Recommendation R04 gives PSHH-102 its own pressure transmitter, so trip I-1 (RV-101 stops when the pick-up pressure stays above 70 kPa g for 3 s) no longer shares PT-102 with PIC-102. Take the PFD of this trip as 0.1 (teaching value).

(a) Can PSHH-102 now be credited as an IPL? (b) Find the new $f_{mit}$. (c) Is TEL met? Give RRF and RRR.

Problem 4.2 · solution

PROBLEM 4.2Independence closes the gap

Part 3$f_{mit} = f_{unmit}\prod PFD_j \qquad RRF = f_{mit}/TEL$
(a) Yes: own sensor, own final elementa plugged PT-102 no longer blinds it
(b) $f_{mit} = 0.05 \times 0.1 \times 0.1 \times 0.01 = 5\times10^{-6}$three independent IPLs
(c) $5\times10^{-6} \le 10^{-5}$: RRF, RRR = NoneTEL met with margin 2

Problem 4.2 · try it

PROBLEM 4.2How good must the new trip be?

Example 3.1$f_{mit} = 5\times10^{-5} \times PFD_{trip}$

Any independent trip with PFD ≤ 0.2 meets TEL: RRR is exactly the PFD the new layer must reach.

Key Takeaways

1

Read the node's intent before you apply a guide word.

2

Score S without safeguards; count them only in L.

3

Check a row on the OTS before you trust its L.

4

Credit only independent layers in LOPA; shared sensors count once.

5

Save the .json every session; hand in .json, report and Excel.
